I want to upgrade the existing application into a productionready text encoder and decoder that reversibly transforms UTF8 text by Base64 encoding it and then multiplying every Base64 charactercode value by the fixed factor 0805, so that users can encode text into a deterministic numeric representation and decode that representation back to the exact original text with complete Unicode support, validation, accessibility, responsive behavior, and clear error handling.

Construct the complete upgrade from beginning to end. Output only the complete, unabridged, productionready source code required for the application. Do not output explanations, architecture notes, pseudocode, placeholders, mock data, dummy content, simulated behavior, TODO comments, omitted sections, ellipses, or partial implementations.

Create exactly two source files:

1. main.zig — the entire backend implementation in one Zig file.
2. index.html — the entire frontend implementation in one HTML file, including all CSS, JavaScript, SVG icons, application views, dialogs, and any subpages or interface states.

Do not create separate CSS, JavaScript, asset, component, template, configuration, or backend files. Do not require a database. Do not require thirdparty APIs, cloud services, authentication systems, external fonts, CDNs, build tools, bundlers, package managers, or runtime dependencies beyond Zig and the Zig standard library.

 Functional transformation specification

Implement a reversible encoding scheme with the following exact behavior:

1. Treat input text as UTF8.
2. Convert the complete UTF8 byte sequence of the input text to standard Base64 using the RFC 4648 alphabet:
   ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/
3. Preserve Base64 padding characters (=) in the Base64 output.
4. For every character in the resulting Base64 string, obtain its numeric Unicode/ASCII code point.
5. Multiply each code point by the decimal integer 805. Treat the userwritten factor 0805 as the integer 805; the leading zero is display notation only and must not produce octal behavior.
6. Serialize the multiplied integer values as decimal integers separated by a single ASCII hyphen (-), with no leading or trailing hyphen and no whitespace.

Example structural format only: value-value-value

The encoder result must therefore be a hyphendelimited decimal numeric string in which each segment represents:

\[
\text{segment} = \text{ASCII code point of one Base64 character} \times 805
\]

Implement decoding as the exact inverse:

1. Accept a hyphendelimited decimal numeric string.
2. Reject empty segments, leading hyphens, trailing hyphens, repeated hyphens, nondecimal characters, signed values, decimal points, whitespace within segments, and values outside the valid transformed range.
3. Parse each segment as an unsigned decimal integer.
4. Require every parsed integer to be evenly divisible by 805.
5. Divide each parsed integer by 805.
6. Require the resulting value to be the ASCII code point of a valid Base64 character from the standard RFC 4648 alphabet or the padding character =.
7. Reconstruct the Base64 string from these recovered characters.
8. Validate the reconstructed Base64 string strictly before decoding it:
    Its length must be a multiple of 4.
    Padding may appear only at the end.
    It may contain at most two = characters.
    No data characters may appear after padding begins.
    It must conform to valid RFC 4648 Base64 structure.
9. Decode the validated Base64 string into bytes.
10. Require the decoded bytes to be valid UTF8.
11. Return the decoded UTF8 text exactly, without normalization, trimming, replacement characters, or data loss.

The operation must be deterministic and lossless. Encoding text and then decoding the emitted result must return exactly the original text, including accents, emoji, line breaks, punctuation, and nonLatin scripts.

Do not claim that this scheme provides encryption, secrecy, cryptographic protection, password protection, or secure obfuscation. Clearly label it in the interface as a reversible text transformation, not encryption.

 Backend requirements: main.zig

Implement a complete HTTP server in Zig using only the Zig standard library. Use a current stable Zig syntax compatible with the latest stable Zig release available at implementation time. Bind to 127.0.0.1 by default and use port 8080 by default. Support optional port configuration through the PORT environment variable, validating that it is an integer from 1 through 65535.

Serve the frontend from the same backend:

 GET / must return the complete index.html application.
 Serve index.html by embedding it into the Zig executable at compile time using @embedFile("index.html").
 Return Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8.
 Return secure, appropriate headers for the local web application:
   X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
   X-Frame-Options: DENY
   Referrer-Policy: no-referrer
   Cache-Control: no-store
   A restrictive Content Security Policy that permits only samedocument inline styles and scripts required by this singlefile frontend, blocks external network connections, blocks framing, and blocks object embedding.
 Implement CORS only if required by the architecture. Because frontend and backend are served from the same origin, do not add permissive wildcard CORS headers.

Implement the following JSON API endpoints:

 POST /api/encode

Request body:

json
{
  "text": "UTF-8 input text"
}


Success response:

json
{
  "ok": true,
  "operation": "encode",
  "base64": "standard Base64 representation",
  "result": "hyphen-delimited multiplied decimal values",
  "inputBytes": 0,
  "outputSegments": 0
}


Requirements:

 Require Content-Type: application/json for JSON API requests.
 Reject bodies larger than 1 MiB with HTTP 413.
 Parse JSON strictly.
 Require that text exists and is a JSON string.
 Preserve the text exactly as submitted.
 Accept an empty text string and encode it successfully. Its Base64 output and final numeric result must both be empty strings, with zero input bytes and zero output segments.
 Return HTTP 200 for successful requests.

 POST /api/decode

Request body:

json
{
  "encoded": "hyphen-delimited multiplied decimal values"
}


Success response:

json
{
  "ok": true,
  "operation": "decode",
  "base64": "reconstructed standard Base64 representation",
  "result": "decoded UTF-8 text",
  "inputSegments": 0,
  "outputBytes": 0
}


Requirements:

 Require Content-Type: application/json.
 Reject bodies larger than 1 MiB with HTTP 413.
 Parse JSON strictly.
 Require that encoded exists and is a JSON string.
 Accept an empty encoded string and decode it successfully. Its reconstructed Base64 string and decoded result must both be empty strings, with zero input segments and zero output bytes.
 Return HTTP 200 for successful requests.

For both endpoints:

 Reject unsupported methods with HTTP 405 and an Allow header.
 Return HTTP 404 for unknown paths.
 Use JSON for all API responses, including all errors.
 Return errors in this exact schema:

json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "MACHINE_READABLE_CODE",
    "message": "Human-readable actionable error message"
  }
}


 Use appropriate HTTP status codes:
   400 for malformed JSON, missing fields, wrong JSON types, invalid transformation input, invalid UTF8, invalid Base64, invalid segment syntax, nondivisible values, and invalid transformed values.
   405 for unsupported HTTP methods.
   413 for bodysize violations.
   415 for missing or invalid request Content-Type.
   404 for unknown routes.
   500 only for unexpected internal server errors.
 Never expose stack traces, allocator internals, raw parser failures, or implementationspecific details to the client.
 Escape all JSON output correctly, including userprovided text containing quotes, backslashes, control characters, Unicode, line breaks, or embedded null bytes.
 Do not log user input, encoded text, or decoded text. Log only concise operational events and unexpected server errors to stderr.
 Handle malformed HTTP requests safely and close connections when necessary.
 Apply reasonable request read timeouts and connection handling so a slow client cannot indefinitely hold the server.
 Process requests safely with bounded memory use and release perrequest allocations.
 Ensure integer parsing cannot overflow and reject overflowed segments rather than wrapping.
 Ensure all URL paths and methods are matched exactly.
 Do not add undocumented endpoints.
 Do not persist user text or transformation results.

Implement the transformation logic as clear reusable Zig functions:

 encodeText
 decodeText
 strict Base64 validation and encoding/decoding helpers
 strict UTF8 validation helper
 JSON request extraction and JSON response writing helpers
 errortoHTTPresponse mapping helpers

Use welldefined error sets or equivalent typed error handling to distinguish validation failures from unexpected failures. Ensure the server remains operational after invalid requests.

 Frontend requirements: index.html

Create a complete, polished, responsive singlepage interface for the application. It must interact only with the two backend API endpoints described above using sameorigin fetch requests. The frontend must not implement an alternate transformation algorithm; the backend is the authoritative implementation.

Use semantic HTML and build every required interface element directly in index.html. Use inline SVG for icons. Do not load external images, icons, fonts, scripts, stylesheets, analytics, tracking code, iframes, or remote resources.

Use the provided design system exactly as the foundation. Define all supplied CSS custom properties in :root, retaining their stated values. Also define any additional aliases needed for practical styling, but do not replace or alter the supplied token values.

Use a dark, precise, minimal interface with:

 Root background: #000000.
 A subtle deep navy topzone gradient based on #09090f.
 Primary text: #f5f5f7.
 Accent/interactions: #0000ff.
 Button text and sharp separators: #ffffff.
 Softmint subdued text: #f6fff9 with controlled opacity where appropriate.
 Native system typography beginning with -apple-system, followed by BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sansserif.
 No external font requests.

The layout must work from 320 px mobile width through large desktop displays. Respect prefers-reduced-motion. Provide visible keyboard focus states. Meet accessible color contrast requirements. Do not rely on color alone to communicate status or errors.

 Application header

Create a fixed or sticky top header with the product name 0805 Base64 Transform.

Include a compact visual mark made from inline SVG or CSS, visually communicating a numeric/text transformation.

Include a clear subtitle: Reversible text transformation — not encryption.

Include an accessible button that opens an information panel or modal describing:

 The exact transformation pipeline: UTF8 text → Base64 → ASCII code point × 805 → hyphendelimited decimal values.
 The exact reverse pipeline for decoding.
 A concise statement that the output is not encrypted and must not be used to protect sensitive data.
 Input constraints and validation behavior.
 The fact that all transformation occurs through the local backend API and is not persisted.

The information interface must be fully keyboard accessible, dismissible with Escape, have appropriate dialog semantics, trap focus while open, return focus to the invoking control when closed, and prevent background interaction while open.

 Workspace

Create a primary workspace containing two mode tabs or segmented controls:

 Encode text
 Decode values

Implement tabs with correct ARIA tab semantics:

 A tablist.
 Each tab has role="tab", an aria-selected value, keyboard support for Left Arrow, Right Arrow, Home, and End.
 Each tab is associated with a tabpanel.
 Only the active panel is shown and keyboard focus transitions correctly.

 Encode panel

Include:

 A labeled multiline input for plain text.
 A live byte counter measured using UTF8 bytes via TextEncoder.
 A primary action button labeled Encode × 805.
 A secondary action to clear the input and result.
 A readable processing state that disables conflicting controls while the request is in flight.
 A Base64 preview area that is shown after a successful encoding operation.
 A final transformedoutput area that is shown after a successful encoding operation.
 An accessible copy button for the transformed output.
 A download button that downloads the transformed output as a .txt file created locally in the browser.
 A status region using aria-live="polite" for success and operational messages.
 An error region using role="alert" for errors.

 Decode panel

Include:

 A labeled multiline input for the hyphendelimited numeric values.
 A live segment counter that treats an empty field as zero segments and otherwise counts hyphenseparated segments.
 A primary action button labeled Decode × 805.
 A secondary action to clear the input and result.
 A readable processing state that disables conflicting controls while the request is in flight.
 A reconstructed Base64 preview area shown after a successful decode.
 A final decodedtext output area shown after success.
 An accessible copy button for the decoded text.
 A download button that downloads the decoded text as a UTF8 .txt file created locally in the browser.
 A status region using aria-live="polite" for success and operational messages.
 An error region using role="alert" for errors.

Use readonly textareas or <pre> elements for outputs so long content remains selectable and readable. Preserve whitespace in decoded output. Support horizontal wrapping or scroll behavior appropriate for long numeric strings without breaking data. Avoid injecting user content with innerHTML; use textContent or textarea values.

 Interaction requirements

 Submit each operation through fetch to /api/encode or /api/decode.
 Send Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8.
 Handle non2xx HTTP responses by safely parsing the documented JSON error schema when available and displaying the returned humanreadable message.
 Handle network failures and malformed server responses with clear userfacing errors.
 Prevent duplicate submissions while an operation is already in progress.
 Abort an inflight request when the user clears its corresponding panel or when the page is unloaded.
 Implement copy behavior using navigator.clipboard.writeText when available, with a secure fallback based on a temporary textarea and document.execCommand("copy"). Report copy success or failure through the associated status region.
 Implement download behavior using a Blob, URL.createObjectURL, a temporary anchor element, and prompt revocation of the object URL after download.
 Do not use browser storage. Do not retain content after refresh.
 Do not send requests until an explicit user action triggers encoding or decoding.
 Do not log text, encoded values, Base64 values, or API responses to the browser console.
 Use clientside checks only for basic usability. Do not duplicate or weaken backend validation.

 Visual details

Use the supplied spacing and radius tokens consistently.

Design the main content as a centered workspace with an appropriate max width and responsive padding. Use nearblack panels, subtle white separators, controlled shadows, and a restrained blue glow around focused or active controls. Maintain generous whitespace without wasting vertical space.

Use clear visual hierarchy:

 Product title and subtitle at the top.
 Mode selection immediately below or integrated into the workspace header.
 Input field and operation controls next.
 Validation/status feedback directly near the operation controls.
 Base64 preview before the final output.
 Final output with prominent but compact copy and download controls.

Style primary actions with the accent blue, white text, clear hover and active states, disabled states, and noncolor status cues. Style secondary controls with restrained transparent or dark surfaces and white borders. Make textarea borders and panel boundaries visible against the black background. Show errors in a highcontrast bordered region with an inline warning SVG icon and text. Show successful operational feedback with an inline check icon plus text, not color alone.

Use no decorative stock imagery. Do not include fake usage statistics, testimonials, user accounts, feature claims, sample data, or marketing content.

 Production completion criteria

The implementation is complete only when all of the following are true:

 zig build-exe main.zig compiles successfully with index.html located in the same directory.
 Running the produced executable serves the application at http://127.0.0.1:8080 unless a valid PORT environment variable overrides the port.
 Both API endpoints correctly process valid UTF8 input, including empty strings, multilingual text, emoji, punctuation, line endings, and large input up to the body limit.
 The encoder emits standard Base64derived decimal segments multiplied exactly by 805.
 The decoder strictly validates input and exactly restores the original UTF8 text for all valid values emitted by the encoder.
 Invalid inputs return documented JSON errors with safe messages and appropriate status codes.
 The frontend has no external runtime dependency and communicates correctly with the local API.
 The interface is responsive, accessible by keyboard, usable with screen readers, and handles loading, success, error, copy, clear, and download states correctly.
 All application behavior is fully implemented in the two required files, with no omitted code or unimplemented functionality.
